verdict.rationale: Mastra is a framework that runs on your own infrastructure. You run its server locally, and agents and workflows can be bundled into your own Node.js/Next.js apps or shipped as standalone endpoints, so Mastra Cloud is optional. The Elastic v2 license noted by the community restricts offering Mastra as a managed service to third parties, but it does not block self-hosting for your own use. missing for 10: a dedicated production self-hosting guide (server/Studio deployment on your own infrastructure), independent hands-on reports of self-hosted production deployments.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Register agents and workflows on one Mastra server, run it locally
Mastra bundles agents and workflows directly into existing React, Next.js and Node.js apps, or ships them as standalone endpoints.
Mastra uses the Elastic v2 license
